headline: New law stops states from banning the sale or possession of ivory, bone, and baleen crafts legally made by Alaska Natives.
what_it_does: States may not ban the sale, trade, barter, transfer, possession, import, or interstate commerce of certain marine mammal products made by Alaska Natives. This covers marine mammal ivory, marine mammal bone, and baleen. It applies only to items legally produced by an Alaska Native as authentic Alaska Native handicrafts or clothing.

who_it_affects.how: They can sell and trade their legally made ivory, bone, and baleen handicrafts and clothing in states that previously banned these items.
States with laws banning marine mammal ivory or similar products can no longer apply those bans to authentic Alaska Native handicrafts and clothing.

who_it_affects.group: Buyers, collectors, and retailers of Alaska Native art
who_it_affects.how: They may buy, own, sell, and move these authentic items across state lines without facing state bans.

when_it_takes_effect: The law was enacted on June 12, 2026; the summary does not give a separate start date.
